newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher, helped by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher, helped by Wall Street.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Tuesday, buoyed by a record rise on Wall Street ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Brokers say a quarter-point rise in U.S. interest rates is priced into financial markets, but a bigger increase could trigger a reaction.

The bourse's blue chip CAC-40 index was up 15.67 points, or 0.76 percent, at 2,082.76 at 0850 GMT, while the CAC-40 September futures contract was 13.5 points higher, bumping up against resistance at 2,085.

Shares in steelmaker Usinor were down two francs at 73.10 after the company reported a 65 percent drop in first-half profit. It came off its lows, however, after forecasting "a less difficult year" in 1997 and a rise in 1997 first-half profit.
Food group Danone rose 1.3 percent to 726 francs after announcing a chilled juice venture with Coca-Cola Foods.
